questions.prompt: Sort these into acids, bases and neutral substances.
questions.explain: Sour foods are acidic; soapy and cleaning substances are usually basic; salt and sugar water are neutral.
Acids turn blue litmus red. Bases turn red litmus blue.

questions.prompt: Match each food to the acid it contains.
questions.explain: Many natural acids are named after where they're found.

questions.prompt: Why should you never identify a lab chemical by tasting it?
options: Some acids and bases are corrosive and poisonous
questions.explain: Strong acids and bases can burn your mouth and skin. Always use indicators.

questions.prompt: A liquid does not change the colour of red litmus OR blue litmus. It is…
questions.explain: No change in either litmus means neutral.

questions.text: Bases that dissolve in water are called ___. Litmus is extracted from ___.
questions.explain: Soluble bases = alkalis; litmus comes from lichens.

questions.prompt: Which are properties of BASES? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: Bases are bitter and soapy and turn red litmus blue. Sourness and turning blue litmus red belong to acids.

options: Some acids are safe to eat, and some bases can burn skin
questions.explain: Food acids are safe; strong acids and strong bases (like drain cleaner) are dangerous.

questions.prompt: Riya dips blue litmus into tomato juice and it turns red. Then she dips red litmus into toothpaste solution and it turns blue. What can she conclude about each? Explain.
questions.modelAnswer: Tomato juice is acidic, because acids turn blue litmus red. Toothpaste is basic, because bases turn red litmus blue.
rubric: Tomato juice is acidic, with the litmus evidence
Toothpaste is basic, with the litmus evidence
questions.explain: Always link your conclusion to the evidence (colour change).
